defaults.permitted_development: A rear or side dormer can be permitted development in Wales where it stays below the existing roof height, avoids the principal elevation, remains within the roof-space volume limits and is kept off the roof edges.

rules.height_rules: No part of the dormer or other roof enlargement should exceed the highest part of the existing roof.
rules.depth_rules: Keep the total roof-space enlargement within 40 cubic metres on a terraced house or 50 cubic metres on any other house.
rules.boundary_rules: A side-facing dormer cannot be within 10.5m of a highway opposite the side elevation. Side-facing dormer windows within 10.5m of an opposite boundary should be obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7m.
rules.roof_rules: Dormers are not permitted on the principal elevation. Other than hip-to-gable work, the dormer should be set back at least 20cm from the eaves. No roof terrace, raised platform or projecting balcony.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

rules.roof_rules: Protected-area controls are tighter in the National Park. Front roof slopes, prominent roof changes and any roof terrace or projecting balcony should be treated cautiously and checked before work starts.
rules.materials_rules: Match the new roof and wall finishes closely to the existing house so the alteration reads as part of the dwelling rather than a separate box.

restrictions.conservation_area: Roof enlargements are not permitted development on protected land in Wales, including conservation areas and national parks. In Bannau Brycheiniog, pre-application advice is the safer route before altering the roof.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on householder permitted development for a listed building. Bannau Brycheiniog expects listed building proposals to be properly evidenced, and listed building consent will usually be required.

rules.permitted_development: A rear or side dormer is often permitted development in Wales where the dormer and any associated roof enlargement remains below the ridge, stays within the roof-space allowance and avoids the principal elevation and projecting balcony route.

rules.height_rules: The dormer should sit within the existing roof height rather than creating a new taller roof form.
rules.depth_rules: Keep the total roof-space enlargement within 40 cubic metres on a terraced house or 50 cubic metres on any other house.
rules.boundary_rules: Where the side roof slope faces a highway or nearby boundary, the 10.5m rules become critical. Side-facing windows within that distance should be obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7m.
rules.roof_rules: The authority states that roof alterations in the National Park require planning permission. That includes roof enlargements, dormers and roof windows, so pre-application advice should be used.
rules.materials_rules: Use external materials that closely relate to the existing house. Obvious mismatches make the roof works look heavier and less subordinate.

restrictions.conservation_area: Eryri already treats roof alterations tightly across the National Park, and conservation area controls add further restriction. Do not assume householder roof rights apply.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent is required for re-roofing or other character-affecting works to a listed building in Eryri. Planning permission may also be needed.

rules.permitted_development: A rear or side dormer can be permitted development in Wales where the dormer and any associated roof enlargement stays below the existing roof height, avoids the principal elevation, remains within the roof-space volume limits and does not create a roof terrace or projecting balcony.

rules.height_rules: No part of the dormer or other roof enlargement should exceed the highest part of the existing roof.
rules.depth_rules: Keep the total roof-space enlargement within 40 cubic metres on a terraced house or 50 cubic metres on any other house.
rules.boundary_rules: A side-facing roof enlargement cannot be within 10.5m of a highway opposite the side elevation. Side-facing windows within 10.5m of an opposite boundary should be obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7m.
rules.roof_rules: Any alteration affecting the roofline, including dormers, should be treated as requiring planning permission in Pembrokeshire Coast National Park.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

restrictions.conservation_area: Roof enlargements are already treated strictly in Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, and conservation area controls add further restriction. Check formally before starting.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on householder permitted development for a listed building. Pembrokeshire Coast guidance expects listed building consent for alterations or extensions affecting character.
